author: reek
body: app-body is the program. Its row says FileSystem.Read and FileSystem.Write and nothing else -- it performs read-text and write-file as bare effect ops and could not name a sector if it wanted to. serve-files is the layer. Its row says Device.Block and nothing else: the `with FileSystem` handler discharges the app's whole family by the dotted lattice (rung 1), and each clause services its op with a fat16 call, whose Device.Block is what the clause bodies re-emit into the layer's own row. That is the attenuation this test exists to pin: the authority to touch the disk lives in the layer, the app carries only the FileSystem grant, and neither signature could absorb the other's without the def boundary rejecting it.

author: reek
body: The runtime half is a real round trip: the app writes NOTE.TXT through the handler, reads it back through the handler, and the bytes must match. The absent path answers through the same handler, so a wrong dispatch cannot hide -- a read that went to the serial port instead of the disk (the read-file builtin trap this op exists to avoid) would hang or answer garbage, never "<absent>".
